topic: A person discovers the tree they planted as a child has been cut down
text: I planted that tree with my own hands, a sapling that barely reached my knee. Years passed, as they always do, and so did I, growing not just in age but in understanding of the world’s ways. That tree, it was a testament, a silent observer of my triumphs and the storms I weathered. When I heard it was gone, the space where it stood now a naked patch of ground, a part of me expected it. Such is the order of things—growth, then decay, or in this case, eradication. Yet, the roots of what it symbolized to me run deep. They cannot be cut so easily. I take solace in the knowledge that its legacy, the lessons it silently imparted, is rooted within me. It’s a small victory, perhaps, but a victory nonetheless.
